issue: When more than one Guidelines provision is sufficiently analogous to an offense under U.S.S.G. § 2X5.1, should appellate courts review the district court's choice of the most analogous guideline de novo or with deference?

sides.position: Review the district court's choice among multiple sufficiently analogous guidelines de novo.
cases: Osborne, 164 F.3d 434, 437-38 (cited in United States v. Betts, 99 F.4th 1048 (7th Cir. 2024))

sides.position: Give the district court's choice among multiple sufficiently analogous guidelines due deference rather than reviewing it de novo.
cases: Osborne, 164 F.3d 434, 437-38 (cited in United States v. Betts, 99 F.4th 1048 (7th Cir. 2024))

quote: Appellate courts differ on whether the district court's decision at this step should be reviewed de novo or given due deference.
cite: United States v. Shamar Betts, 99 F.4th 1048 (7th Cir. 2024)
